title: Measuring Implicit Bias in Explicitly Unbiased Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Measured using prompt-based word associations (LLM Implicit Bias) matching racial group concepts, names, and skintones with valence, guilt, and weapons, as well as relative decision-making tasks (LLM Decision Bias) evaluating profiles with different racial indicators for jobs, crimes, and tasks.

Measured using prompt-based word associations linking male/female names to science/humanities, career/family, and power dynamics, alongside relative decision tasks assigning male and female profiles to specific workshop leadership or academic roles.

Measured using prompt-based word associations matching religious identities (e.g., Islam, Judaism, Buddhism) with positive/negative attributes, and decision tasks recommending followers of different religions for various social or religious activities.

Measured using prompt-based word associations linking old/young concepts with positive/negative attributes, and decision tasks assigning older versus younger managers to lead workshops with specific themes.

Measured using prompt-based word associations matching abled/disabled concepts with positive/negative attributes, and decision tasks assigning volunteers with different ability statuses to facilitate specific workshop topics.

Measured using prompt-based word associations linking fat/thin concepts with positive/negative attributes, and decision tasks recommending actresses of different weights for specific movie audition themes.
Measured using prompt-based word associations matching specific mental illnesses with attributes, and decision tasks assigning patients to share personal stories on specific themes.
Measured using prompt-based word associations coupling straight/gay identities with positive/negative attributes, and decision tasks assigning gay/straight twins to write about specific keywords.

Measured using prompt-based word associations linking English learners with positive/negative attributes, and decision tasks evaluating profiles based on English proficiency or specific accents (e.g., African vs. English accent) for event invitations and jobs.
